summary: Today’s pulse tracks Supreme Court revives controversial US data system for citizenship checks, Internet restricted after fighting breaks out in Ethiopia's Tigray region, and No general election before 2029, Andy Burnham says. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are election, general, and labour. In the background, Ed Sheeran’s concerts in Massachusetts canceled due to severe weather and Protests erupt as Netanyahu gives inflammatory UN speech - The Latest keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Supreme Court revives controversial US data system for citizenship checks
headlines.description: The system uses citizenship information and other sensitive data to filter alleged non-citizen voting.

headlines.title: Internet restricted after fighting breaks out in Ethiopia's Tigray region
headlines.description: During the two-year civil war in Tigray, the region was totally cut off from the outside world.

headlines.title: No general election before 2029, Andy Burnham says
headlines.description: Prime minister quashes speculation that Labour’s revival in the polls could prompt early contest Andy Burnham has said he will not call a general election before 2029, after days of speculation that Labour’s revival in the polls could tempt him to call an early contest. The prime minister was repeatedly questioned on the prospect during a round of broadcast interviews to regional media on Friday.

headlines.title: Ed Sheeran’s concerts in Massachusetts canceled due to severe weather
headlines.description: The singer was set to perform at Gillette Stadium as part of his Loop tour, which faces backlash over Macklemore’s removal following his pro-Palestinian comments Ed Sheeran’s concerts at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, have been canceled due to severe weather, adding further complication to a tour embroiled in controversy. On Friday, Sheeran’s tour promoter, Messina Touring, said : “Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium.”

headlines.title: Protests erupt as Netanyahu gives inflammatory UN speech - The Latest
headlines.description: More than 100 people were arrested at large protests against the Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the UN general assembly. Susan Sarandon, Chelsea Manning and Caleb Hearon were among the famous faces arrested. Inside the assembly hall, Netanyahu faced a mass walkout as he took to the stage. Then, in an inflammatory address, he claimed Israel’s war in Gaza was the ‘opposite of a genocide’ and labelled the New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani, antisemitic. Lucy Hough speaks to UK global editor Devika Bhat – watch on YouTube – Listen to Thursday’s episode of Stateside with Kai and Carter on whether Netanyahu has lost America here

headlines.title: Healey appoints Labour manifesto writer, adding to election speculation
headlines.description: Exclusive: Economist Ravinder Athwal, who worked in Keir Starmer’s team, is poached from Flint Global Ravinder Athwal, the economist who wrote Labour’s 2024 manifesto, is taking on a senior role as an adviser to John Healey, in a move likely to fuel speculation about an early general election. The chancellor is keen to strengthen his team before the critical budget on 28 October, as the economy is buffeted by high oil prices and rising government borrowing costs .

headlinePool.title: Alberta’s ‘rat patrol’ ramps up operations as vermin makes inroads in province
headlinePool.description: ‘Rat-free’ Canadian province recently took a verminous hit when a dead rodent turned up in town of Bowden For more than seven decades, residents of Alberta have shared something in common with Antarctica and the high Arctic: all locations are officially free of rats. But on Thursday the Canadian province’s reputation as a firewall against rodent infestation took a hit when the town of Bowden announced the discovery of a dead rat and called on the province’s “rat patrol” to investigate.

headlinePool.title: Why Ed Miliband has embraced his ‘awkward dad’ image in viral TikTok video
headlinePool.description: About 1.5 million people have watched footage of foreign secretary that capitalises on social media’s love of a cringe moment It sparked delight among the diehard Milifans and a begrudging smile from those less keen on the foreign secretary, but a viral video of Ed Miliband has – possibly – confirmed his status as the internet’s awkward dad. About 1.5 million people have viewed an interaction between Miliband and the TikTok personality Feroz Khan on the streets of New York, during which the digital content creator asks Miliband a series of questions including his name, job and his top piece of advice.

headlinePool.title: Novelist accused of using AI to write book removed from French prize list
headlinePool.description: Thélyson Orélien had been in the running to win a top literary prize before the AI claim emerged on social media The organisers of France’s most prestigious literary prize said they had removed a critically acclaimed novel by a Canadian-Haitian writer from the longlist after an anonymous online account claimed the book was “almost entirely” written by AI. The Académie Goncourt, a Paris-based literary organisation, said on Friday its decision to withdraw Thélyson Orélien’s novel C’était ça ou mourir (It Was That or Die) was “driven by the desire to preserve the integrity of the Goncourt prize and the academy itself, whose central role is to promote and honour literature written by women and men”.

headlinePool.title: Woman who accused Jay-Z of sexual assault says her claims were false
headlinePool.description: On Thursday, the woman identified as Jane Doe filed a declaration in Manhattan federal court stating that all of her original claims against the rapper were false.

headlinePool.title: Ketanji Brown Jackson criticizes supreme court’s handling of emergency docket
headlinePool.description: The justice called out her colleagues in a speech she made at the UDC school of law, hours after Trump filed his latest request US supreme court justice Ketanji Brown Jackson acknowledged serious concerns about her colleagues’ handling of emergency requests, the method Donald Trump often uses to seek approval from the court. Jackson, one of the three liberal members of the supreme court, criticized the justices’ willingness to issue rulings via the “shadow docket”, saying it undermines the public’s faith in the judicial system.

headlinePool.title: ‘These efforts have not gone too well’: your questions on how money will influence midterm elections answered
headlinePool.description: Who are the groups backing candidates in the midterms – and why? Joseph Gedeon, Dara Kerr and Chris Stein answered your questions Sign up to The Stakes newsletter: your weekly guide to the US midterms Nola67 asks Alex Vindman had $16 million fundraised during his losing campaign against Angie Nixon [to be the Democrat’s Senate nominee in Florida]. Will he be giving that money to Nixon now, and is she getting more funding help from the national Democratic Party? Joseph: Our understanding is that he’s using his sizeable war chest to boost Democrats across the country, and to the Florida Democratic state party, though not Nixon herself. He announced back in August that he’d be sending $250k to the Democratic Senatorial Campaign committee and candidates like Abdul El Sayed in Michigan, Troy Jackson in Maine, Roy Cooper in North Carolina, Sherrod Brown in Ohio, Charles Booker in Kentucky, and more. In Florida, he says he invested $400k to the state democratic party, though not directly to Nixon herself. It seems like the Senate Majority PAC, led by Chuck Schumer and meant to boost Democrats to the Senate, are steering clear of Nixon’s campaign – it seems they don’t find that one winnable, and don’t want to put the investment into it. Dara: Theoretically AI could be used for recovering debt for investors for the government, but given the mistakes and bias the technology still has it would likely need human oversight for this work. It’s more feasible that AI will be used as a tool to help identify trends and organize material, but then people would have to direct this work and keep tabs on the technology to ensure all rules and regulations are being followed.

headlinePool.title: White House television pool resumes after banned news outlets regain access
headlinePool.description: Trump’s media ban resulted in an effective TV blackout of coverage of the president during the UN general assembly The primary White House television pool has resumed filming administration events after a court ruling temporarily overturned a Trump administration ban on CNN a day earlier. In an unprecedented move, the pool – which also includes NBC, ABC, CBS and Fox News – ceased recording and transmitting White House footage on Monday, in solidarity with CNN, MS Now and Politico, which had been banned by Trump from the building over what he said was “their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS.”

headlinePool.title: Pope Leo warns of AI threat to humanity at start of three-day France visit
headlinePool.description: Pontiff says artificial intelligence must remain at service of people in first official papal visit to country in 18 years Pope Leo has warned against losing humanity in a “paradise of machines” as he addressed global concerns over the dangers of artificial intelligence at the start of a three-day visit to France. “If we are to avoid losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines invading and conditioning our daily lives, there is an urgent need for people to be educated in ethical discernment, capable of seeing what is morally right,” he said in a speech at the Elysée.

headlinePool.title: There's a global pandemic treaty that's signed -- and in 'limbo.' What's the holdup?
headlinePool.description: The treaty aims to help the countries of the world prepare for — and defeat — any future pandemic. Why hasn't it gone into effect?
